newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 30.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Wednesday:
* On Tuesday, the Dow Jones rose by 34.29 points to 6,007.02. PLDT's ADR jumped $ 1 7/8 to $59 1/8.
* The peso closed at 26.284 to a U.S.dollar from 26.285.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange index closed at 2,904.41, up 52.25.
* The Philippine interbank call loan rate unchanged at 11.09375 percent.

* Stock brokerage Sun Hung Kai Securities said with the index having recovered 25 percent of the plunge in the last two days, the market may pause at current levels with a chance of filling the gap of 2,963-2,942 which formed on Monday. The local market will take its cue from the reaction of Wall Street on U.S. economic indicators coming out on Wednesday and Friday and the release of San Miguel Corp on Thursday. The next strong support of the Phisix stands at around the 2,750 level, Sun Hung Kai said.

* PLDT reported on Wednesday that its net income in the first nine months of 1996 rose to 4.670 billion pesos from the previous year's 4.693 billion pesos which included a 1.154 billion peso extraordinary gain from the sale of its stake in subsidiary Pilipino Telephone Corp.
"Without this unusual gain in 1995, net income in 1996 would be 32 percent higher over that of 1995," the company said in a statement.

* Socioeconomic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said the government had revised upward its inflation target for the year to an average of 8.7 percent from 8.5 due to the increases in domestic oil prices and the expected increased consumer spending this Christmas.

* RFM Corp chairman Jose Concepcion said on Tuesday the firm expected a net income of 500 million to 550 million pesos in 1996 due to an upsurge in sales during the fourth quarter. The projected net income for 1996 is lower than the 1995 figure of 620.6 million pesos. For the nine-months period ending September, 1996, RFM reported its net income dropped to 346.8 million pesos from 419.5 million.

* Cellular phone firm Pilipino Telephone Corp is eyeing a 1.4 billion peso net income in 1997, 40 percent higher than the 1996 projected profits of one billion pesos, a top company official told Reuters on Tuesday. Earlier, Piltel downgraded its 1996 net income forecast of 1.16 billion pesos due to illegal calls expected to result in a 300 million peso revenue loss by the end of the year.
